content.title: JavaScript Gives Instructions a Shape
content.hook: A programming language gives you a way to describe work precisely. In JavaScript, that work is built from small pieces. Some pieces are values. Some pieces are expressions that produce values.
content.context: For now, ignore browsers and buttons. JavaScript can be studied as a language on its own. Today we are learning to read the language before we try to make large programs.
goals: Understand that JavaScript programs are built from values and expressions that produce results.

content.title: What is a value?
content.text:
A value is a piece of information a program can work with.

Examples:

```js
42
"Forge"
true
````

The number 42 is a value. The text "Forge" is a value. `true` is a value.

content.question:
What value does this expression produce?

```js
2 + 3
```

feedback.correct: The `+` operator combines the two numbers, producing the number `5`.
feedback.incorrect: The `+` operator combines the two numbers, producing the number `5`.

content.title: Expressions do work
content.text:
An **expression** is code that produces a value.

```js
10
10 + 5
5 > 2
```

The first expression produces `10`. The second produces `15`. The third produces `true`.

This gives us a useful reading habit: when you see an expression, ask, **"What value comes out?"**

content.question:
Predict the result before checking it:

```js
7 * 2
```

feedback.correct: Multiplication gives `14`. Prediction first; execution second.
feedback.incorrect: Multiplication gives `14`. Prediction first; execution second.

activities.title: Change one piece
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt:
Start with:

```js
10 + 5
```

Change only `5` to `8`. What should the expression produce now?


The point is not arithmetic speed. The point is seeing that changing one input changes the resulting value.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.

feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.question: Which sentence best describes an expression?

options.text: It is any file in a project.
It is code that produces a value.
It is only text inside quotes.

feedback.correct: Functions can contain expressions, but an expression is the smaller idea: code that produces a value.
feedback.incorrect: Functions can contain expressions, but an expression is the smaller idea: code that produces a value.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Read JavaScript from the inside out: identify the values, then ask what each expression produces.
**Senior habit:** Before changing code, predict what the existing expression produces. If you cannot predict it, slow down before editing.
nextSteps: Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
